section_summary: This section contains Federal Communications Commission intercepts of Domei news broadcasts and international radio traffic, together with State Department, Office of War Information, and Netherlands Embassy correspondence about protecting the secrecy of Allied monitoring. The broadcasts carry Japanese wartime propaganda and reports on the Pacific, China, Southeast Asia, India, Europe, occupied territories, economic controls, and colonial independence movements. The section also includes romanized Japanese transmissions, French-language Domei material, and private commercial or personal radiograms between Argentina and Japan.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on the Solomon Islands naval campaign
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from Japanese station JUO/JAU2
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. radio monitors
subfiles.about: A Japanese propaganda analysis presents successive phases of American naval strategy in the South Pacific and emphasizes the importance of production and supply lines.
subfiles.summary: The transmission claims that American battleship, carrier, and land-based-air strategies successively failed around Pearl Harbor and the Solomon Islands. It lists purported American and Japanese ship and aircraft losses and describes opposing base networks extending from Australia and New Guinea to the northern Solomons and Rabaul. The report concludes that long-distance supply, industrial production, and replacement from the American mainland will determine the campaign.

subfiles.title: FCC cover letter forwarding additional Domei intercepts
subfiles.from: S. W. Norman, Acting Chief, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards additional copies of intercepted Domei press material to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: FCC cover letter by special messenger forwarding more Domei intercepts (FCC 12718, State 894.76).

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Burma, Philippine independence, India, China, and occupied Southeast Asia
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUO/JAU2
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. radio monitors
subfiles.about: A sequence of Domei reports covers Axis-sponsored independence, Indian nationalism, Japanese naval inspections, counterinsurgency in China, and occupation administration in Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: Reports quote Ba Maw and Chang Ching-hui, describe José Laurel's work on a Philippine constitution, and contrast Gandhi's nonviolent movement with Subhas Chandra Bose's armed campaign. Other items report Admiral Zengo Yoshida's inspection tour, Jirō Saitō's anti-British statement, Japanese operations in Shanxi, and Shōzō Murata's praise for occupation administration in Java and Celebes. The transmission is strongly propagandistic and promotes the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese Domei intercept of August 7
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.about: A romanized Japanese transmission discusses wartime operational secrecy and a conference of German leaders in Berlin.
subfiles.summary: Romanized Domei intercept of August 7: Japanese secrecy about losses, and a Berlin conference of Hitler, Göring, Ribbentrop and others; untranslated and partly garbled.

subfiles.title: Netherlands Ambassador's letter warning about disclosure of intercepted broadcasts
subfiles.from: Alexander Loudon, Netherlands Ambassador
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: The Netherlands ambassador forwards an Australian memorandum warning against using Japanese local broadcasts in Allied propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Netherlands Ambassador asks Hornbeck to alert American authorities that public references to monitored broadcasts could alert Japan and end a valuable intelligence source.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on protecting Japanese local-broadcast monitoring in the Netherlands Indies
subfiles.from: Netherlands or Australian authorities
subfiles.about: The memorandum urges that American broadcasts and publications not reveal Allied reception of Japanese local broadcasts from the Netherlands Indies.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Japanese local broadcasts from Bandung, Makassar and Batavia received in Australia yield intelligence; public use made Japanese broadcasts more guarded; cites Radio San Francisco's Makassar mention and asks no further references.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledgment to the Netherlands Ambassador
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges the ambassador's letter and promises to inform interested authorities.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks the Netherlands Ambassador for the Australian memorandum and will pass it to appropriate authorities.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck follow-up on the Radio San Francisco disclosure
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck
subfiles.about: Hornbeck explains how Radio San Francisco learned about the Japanese station at Makassar and reports that the matter is being addressed.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says the information came from a Japanese shortwave broadcast monitored on the West Coast after an earlier Australian report was kept confidential, and the Knickerbocker Weekly had also mentioned Dutch monitoring; Radio San Francisco is being notified.

subfiles.title: Current Information note on referral to the OWI San Francisco office
subfiles.from: M. S. Myers, Division of Current Information
subfiles.about: Myers reports that the monitoring-security concern was shown to George Taylor of the Office of War Information.
subfiles.summary: Taylor agrees Hornbeck's point is sound and will raise it with OWI San Francisco; Myers adds monitoring of several stations was never quoted on air.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck memorandum identifying the central monitoring-security question
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck
subfiles.about: Hornbeck argues that the key issue is whether the Allies should disclose awareness of the Makassar station and Dutch monitoring in Australia.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck accepts Taylor's explanation of the June 6 broadcast but says the key question is whether Americans or Dutch should publicize the station and its interception.

subfiles.title: Current Information transmittal of George Taylor's memorandum
subfiles.from: M. S. Myers, Division of Current Information
subfiles.about: Myers forwards an OWI memorandum responding to the Netherlands ambassador's complaint.
subfiles.summary: Current Information sends George Taylor's memorandum, chief of OWI's Seventh Region, as a self-explanatory answer to the Dutch complaint.

subfiles.title: OWI memorandum explaining the Makassar broadcast reference
subfiles.from: George Taylor, Office of War Information
subfiles.about: Taylor explains the source and handling of Radio San Francisco's statement that Japan operated a broadcasting station at Makassar.
subfiles.summary: Taylor confirms a June 6 Malay broadcast mentioned Makassar; the information came from Australia for background, was kept confidential until heard on Japanese shortwave, and the Knickerbocker Weekly had publicized Dutch monitoring.

subfiles.title: Netherlands Embassy acknowledgment of Hornbeck's explanation
subfiles.from: Netherlands chargé d’affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: The Netherlands Embassy acknowledges and appreciates Hornbeck's explanation of how Radio San Francisco obtained the Makassar information.
subfiles.summary: Netherlands chargé, with Ambassador Loudon absent, thanks Hornbeck for clarifying how Radio San Francisco learned of Makassar broadcasts.

subfiles.title: FCC cover letter forwarding Domei and Argentina–Japan intercepts
subfiles.from: S. W. Norman, Acting Chief, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards Domei press intercepts and copies of radio traffic between Argentina and Japan.
subfiles.summary: FCC cover letter by special messenger forwarding Domei news broadcasts and intercepted Argentina-Japan communications.

subfiles.title: Four-page romanized Japanese Domei intercept of August 9
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.about: A romanized Japanese broadcast discusses the Greater East Asia war, wartime clothing controls, and Subhas Chandra Bose's strategy for Indian independence.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept of August 9: the war as building a new East Asian order, Allied production in the South Pacific, simplified clothing and ration-point changes, and Bose on Britain's dependence on India, the INA and differences with Gandhi.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese Domei intercept on German weapons, barter, Australia, and Gibraltar
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.about: A Japanese-language transmission carries foreign-news items about German armaments and barter, Australian defenses, and a fire at Gibraltar.
subfiles.summary: The broadcast describes a new German heavy weapon, a Hanover department-store barter exchange, and alleged difficulty recruiting settlers or defenders in northern Australia. It also reports that stored fuel caught fire near Gibraltar harbor and suggests sabotage as a possible cause. The romanized text is incomplete and heavily garbled.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese account of an air raid on Funafuti
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.about: A Japanese correspondent gives a dramatic first-person account of an air attack on Funafuti in the Ellice Islands.
subfiles.summary: The report portrays Japanese naval aviators approaching Funafuti through clouds and antiaircraft fire. It describes repeated attacks, searchlights or gun flashes, bombing runs, and shouted course corrections from the aircraft crew. The narrative is designed to celebrate Japanese naval aviation and fighting spirit.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese intercept on naval aviation and Indian independence
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports Wichit Wathakan's inspection of Japanese naval aviation schools and a Bangkok Chinese-community declaration supporting Indian independence.
subfiles.summary: Intercept: the Thai foreign minister visits Tsuchiura and Kasumigaura air units; anniversary of Gandhi's arrest; Bangkok Chinese associations back the INA and rapid independence.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese foreign-news intercept of August 12
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.about: Domei reports on the split between Gandhian and armed Indian nationalists, bombing in Britain, flooding in India, and shortages in the Middle East.
subfiles.summary: Intercept of August 12: even Gandhi's followers moving toward armed revolution, German raids on Plymouth and Bournemouth, Indian floods, and fuel and food shortages in Egypt, Syria, Palestine and Iran, from an Axis perspective.

subfiles.title: Romanized Japanese intercept on Pacific combat, food production, and Nanjing economic controls
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.about: The transmission combines Japanese communiqués on fighting near Kolombangara and the Solomons with domestic agricultural policy and economic measures in Nanjing and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Intercept: an Imperial Headquarters claim of sinking a destroyer and air operations over Shortland and Rendova, calls for more wheat and barley, and Nanjing compulsory purchases and financial controls to restrain inflation.

subfiles.title: Intercepted Argentina–Japan commercial and personal radiograms
subfiles.from: Private and commercial correspondents using Argentina–Japan radio circuits
subfiles.to: Addressees in Argentina, Japan, Europe, and the Americas; intercepted by FCC monitors
subfiles.about: The pages compile garbled multilingual press, commercial, and personal radiograms routed through Argentina–Japan communications channels.
subfiles.summary: Messages in Spanish, Italian, French, and English concern merchandise, credit, shipping documentation, travel permission, health, births, anniversaries, condolences, and family news. Correspondents and destinations include Buenos Aires, Tucumán, Milan, Lausanne, Mendoza, La Chaux-de-Fonds, Lima, Caracas, Havana, and other cities. Signal quality is poor, leaving many names and passages uncertain.

subfiles.title: Japanese-language Domei intercept on barter, Australian defenses, and Gibraltar
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JHL/JUP3
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: This intercept duplicates or clarifies reports about German barter arrangements, Australian home defense, and a Gibraltar fuel fire.
subfiles.summary: One report describes a Hanover exchange where civilians barter unwanted household items for necessities. Another mocks an alleged Australian plan to recruit settlers or defenders for the sparsely populated north. A final item describes a fire among fuel tanks near Gibraltar and speculates that guerrillas or saboteurs penetrated strict security.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Philippine administration, Nanjing diplomacy, and Celebes cotton
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUO/JAU2
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports on Filipino political tours, José Laurel's governmental work, Nanjing diplomacy, and cotton production in Celebes.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Leon Guinto and Filipino visitors to lecture in Luzon, Laurel meets governors and completes the constitution, Wang Ching-wei returns to Nanjing, Woermann meets Shigemitsu, and Sulawesi cotton growing.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Nanjing cotton controls, Allied conferences, and the European war
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: Domei summarizes a Nippon Times editorial on cotton controls and presents Axis-oriented coverage of the Churchill–Roosevelt conference and fighting in Europe.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Nanjing's compulsory acquisition of cotton yarn to curb speculation, Churchill's party traveling to Canada, Anglo-Soviet divisions, and Axis claims on Sicily, the Soviet front, Gibraltar and the battleship Littorio.

subfiles.title: Domei intercept on Mengjiang operations, Sumatra currency exchange, diplomacy, and the Kurils
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: The broadcast combines Japanese military claims in Inner Mongolia with reports on Sumatra exchange offices, Nanjing cotton policy, diplomatic visits, and an American raid on the Kurils.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Japanese claims of encircling Communists near Yenking, new guilder-Straits dollar exchange offices in Riau, Yoshizawa meeting Decoux, Wichit's Nikkō visit, and repelling American aircraft over the Chishima Islands.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Japan, Allied diplomacy, and Chinese counterinsurgency
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: The transmission praises Japanese wartime morale, attacks Allied diplomacy, and lists claimed Japanese successes against Chinese Communist forces.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Vicente Guzman calls Japan calm and confident, items on Yoshizawa and Decoux, a Kuril appearance by American aircraft, the coming Churchill-Roosevelt conference, and claimed Communist losses in four provinces.

subfiles.title: French-language Domei intercept on Southeast Asia, Inner Mongolia, and North China
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, French-language service from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: French-language broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: French-language Domei reports cover Thai and Japanese official travel, military operations in Inner Mongolia and North China, and currency exchange in Sumatra.
subfiles.summary: French Domei intercept: Pairot Jaiyanama leaves Hsinking, Uchigasaki reaches Makassar, claims of Communist encirclement and casualties across North China, Riau exchange offices, and Shigemitsu meeting German and Italian ambassadors.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Hebei operations and Malayan students in Japan
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: After reporting Japanese military claims in Hebei, the broadcast profiles five Malayan students receiving education and cultural training in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The opening item gives claimed casualty, prisoner, weapons, and installation totals from Japanese operations against Chongqing-aligned forces in Hebei. The remainder celebrates five Malayan students sponsored by Marquis Yoshichika Tokugawa, describing their Japanese-language studies, schools, domestic routines, and adaptation to Japanese food and customs. The students are portrayed as future leaders who will return to Malaya and teach Japanese values and strength.

subfiles.title: Domei press intercept on Axis diplomacy, China, shipping, Italy, and the Kurils
subfiles.from: Domei News Agency, broadcast from JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Broadcast audience; intercepted by U.S. monitors
subfiles.about: The transmission reports Japanese-Axis diplomatic discussions, attacks Allied conference policy, and covers Chinese operations, experimental shipping, Italy, and an air raid on the Kurils.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Shigemitsu meets Ambassadors Stahmer and Indelli; Tokyo Shimbun reads Allied difficulties into the Churchill-Roosevelt conference; claims against Chinese forces; a new coastal ship; Italy staying with Germany; three B-17s claimed over the Kurils.
